# 1 Clement Chapter 40 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 40 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_040_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 40

**40:1** Since all this is clear to us and we have looked deeply into God's knowledge, we ought to carry out everything the Master has commanded — in an orderly way, at the times he has appointed.

**40:2** He directed that offerings and services should be performed — not haphazardly or without order, but at set times and seasons.

**40:3** He himself determined, by his supreme will, both where and through whom he wanted these to be performed — so that everything would be done in holiness according to his good pleasure and be acceptable to him.

**40:4** Those who bring their offerings at the proper times are accepted and blessed — because they follow the Master's regulations and do not go wrong.

**40:5** The high priest has his own appointed duties; the priests have their own designated place; the Levites have their own assigned service; the layperson is governed by the rules that apply to laypeople.

---

*PNEUMA makes the ordered-worship argument accessible, emphasizing that the divine order is both deliberate (v. 3) and beneficial (v. 4).*
